source_page_metadata.description: Oishii strain guide covering genetics, THC, effects, flavor, terpenes, medical uses, and growing information for this Flavor Pack #7 × Moonbow 112 F2 #60 hybrid.

section_headings: What are the genetics of Oishii?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Flavor Pack #7 × Moonbow 112 F2 #60
Breeder: Archive Seed Bank
THC Content: 18–31%
CBD Content: Usually below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , linalool , pinene
Primary Flavors: Candy, citrus, tangerine, lime, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 63–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: late October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Oishii is built around contrast. Sweet citrus and Z-style candy may arrive first, but the flower does not stay in dessert territory for long. Perfumed incense, skunk, earth, Kush-like gas, and floral spice emerge underneath, creating the kind of aroma that changes noticeably as a bud is broken apart. The Japanese name translates roughly to “delicious,” and Archive Seed Bank chose it for a cultivar specifically bred around flavor intensity rather than a simple pursuit of THC numbers. Mature flowers can develop light-green surfaces streaked with purple, bright orange pistils, and a thick layer of resin that hints at why Oishii has also developed a strong reputation among hash and solventless concentrate producers.

Archive Seed Bank created the strain by pairing Flavor Pack #7 with Moonbow 112 F2 #60. The breeder describes the project as essentially a Moonbow backcross, because Moonbow genetics are present on both sides of the family tree. That concentration of related ancestry reinforces the candy-gas qualities associated with Moonbow while allowing the Flavor Pack selection to introduce a stronger incense, perfume, skunk, and OG-like dimension. Archive lists the original release as regular seed with a flowering window of 63 to 70 days.
Genetics and Lineage

Flavor Pack #7 forms the maternal side of Oishii and traces to Hollywood Pure Kush crossed with Moonbow. That combination is important because it brings old-school Kush depth into a family otherwise strongly associated with bright candy terpenes. Hollywood Pure Kush contributes earthy, musky, fuel-heavy qualities, while Moonbow adds the sweeter Z-influenced fruit and citrus characteristics. Archive selected Flavor Pack #7 specifically for its unusually forceful perfumed incense, potpourri, and skunk profile, traits that remain obvious in well-grown Oishii.

Moonbow 112 F2 #60 reinforces that aromatic foundation from the other side. Moonbow itself comes from Z genetics paired with Do-Si-Dos , combining fruit-candy intensity with OGKB , Cookies , and Face Off OG influence. Because Flavor Pack already contains Moonbow ancestry, crossing it to a selected Moonbow F2 compresses that family rather than introducing a completely unrelated parent. Archive explicitly describes the result as concentrating Moonbow’s candy-gas characteristics into a more focused genetic package.

That structure explains why commercial cuts can emphasize different aspects of the same family. Tower Three’s Oishii selection leans toward earth, musk, Z candy, clementine, tangerine, and lemon sweetness, while other cultivators emphasize floral perfume, lime, skunk, or OG gas. The underlying theme remains remarkably consistent: bright candy and citrus positioned against a darker, more pungent background.
Effects and Experience

The first phase can feel deceptively gentle. Sweet flavor and a smooth onset may suggest a lightweight hybrid, yet the mental effects tend to accumulate rather than arrive all at once. Early changes often include brighter mood, increased sensory interest, and a pleasant cerebral buzz that can make conversation, music, gaming, or creative activities more engaging. Rather than producing a sharp rush, the weed frequently develops as a gradual uplift followed by a stronger awareness that the THC has taken hold.

Physical relaxation becomes clearer as the session progresses. The body begins to feel looser while the cerebral edge settles into a calmer, dreamier state. Experienced concentrate producer Wojo describes Oishii as deceptively strong and notes that the effect can creep in after the lighter fruit flavor creates an initially manageable impression. JAR similarly characterizes its selected flower as uplifting at first before becoming mellow and soothing.

Potency varies considerably. JAR has listed flower around 18–23% THC, laboratory-tested Sanctuary batches have measured about 20–22.3% total THC, while a Tower Three retail batch reached 31.3%. Those differences make a universal THC figure misleading. Stronger examples can become substantially heavier and may produce dry mouth, slowed concentration, dizziness, or anxiety in consumers who exceed their comfortable dose.
Medical Benefits

Oishii has not been evaluated as an individual medical marijuana treatment in controlled clinical trials, so its reputation should not be interpreted as evidence that the strain treats specific diseases. Its combination of initial mood elevation and later body relaxation may nevertheless appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer THC-dominant flower for temporary stress relief, appetite stimulation, minor discomfort, or help settling into an evening routine.

The cultivar’s gradual progression may be particularly attractive to people who dislike weed that produces immediate couch-lock. Moderate use can preserve some mental engagement while reducing physical tension, whereas larger amounts may become considerably more sedating. Patients sensitive to THC should be cautious because stronger commercial cuts can reach very high potency.

Terpene chemistry also changes between growers. Tested Oishii flower has shown limonene, linalool, caryophyllene, pinene, and myrcene in different proportions. One Tower Three batch contained 3.18% total terpenes with limonene as the largest component, while other selections emphasize pinene and linalool. These compounds contribute to aroma and sensory character, but they should not be treated as proven predictors of a specific medical outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma begins with candy but quickly becomes stranger and more complex. Tangerine, clementine, lime, lemon candy, and Z-style fruit sweetness can rise from the flower immediately after grinding. Beneath those brighter notes sit damp earth, musk, floral perfume, skunk, incense, and an unmistakable gas component. Archive specifically selected the Flavor Pack side for a perfumed incense and potpourri character strong enough to perfume an entire room.

On the palate, citrus sweetness often arrives first. Tangerine and lime may give way to sugary candy before heavier Kush, skunk, and earthy flavors appear on the exhale. Some phenotypes produce a pronounced floral quality, while others lean more aggressively toward gas. Tower Three describes its selected cut as finishing with a lingering Z-style coating across the palate, illustrating how strongly the Moonbow ancestry can dominate a well-grown example.
Growing Information

Archive Seed Bank provides a verified indoor flowering window of 63–70 days, placing Oishii at roughly nine to ten weeks from the start of bloom. The original release was sold as regular seed, so growers hunting through seed stock should expect genuine phenotype variation rather than every plant reproducing the same commercial cut.

Selected examples show attractive flower structure, including light-green buds, purple coloration, orange pistils, and heavy resin coverage. Tower Three’s cut demonstrates how strongly the plant can express both its Z and Do-Si-Dos sides visually and aromatically. Dense resin production makes airflow and humidity management increasingly important as flowers mature, particularly in crowded indoor canopies.

Archive has not published standardized indoor or outdoor yield figures, so precise grams-per-square-meter estimates found elsewhere should be treated skeptically. For growers selecting from seed, aroma intensity, resin coverage, flower structure, and the balance between candy and incense-gas traits are likely more meaningful selection criteria than sheer weight.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Oishii?
Oishii is Flavor Pack #7 × Moonbow 112 F2 #60. Archive Seed Bank describes it as a Moonbow-focused backcross because Moonbow genetics also appear within the Flavor Pack side of the pedigree.
Who bred the Oishii strain?
Archive Seed Bank created Oishii. The breeder continues to list the cultivar in its official strain library and has also used Oishii in newer crosses.
Is Oishii indica or sativa?

Oishii is a hybrid. Some commercial selections are described as indica leaning because the later effects can become deeply relaxing, although the opening phase may feel cerebral, euphoric, and surprisingly engaging.
How strong is Oishii weed?

Strength varies substantially by grower and phenotype. Documented commercial examples range from about 18% THC into the low-30% range, so consumers should rely on the laboratory results for the specific batch rather than a single strain-wide number.
What does Oishii taste like?

Expect candy, tangerine, lime, lemon, floral perfume, skunk, earth, incense, and gas. Some selections lean strongly toward Z-style citrus candy, while others emphasize the darker Kush and skunk qualities.
Final Thoughts on Oishii

Oishii succeeds because Archive Seed Bank did more than cross two fashionable names. By bringing Flavor Pack #7 together with Moonbow 112 F2 #60, the breeder concentrated related Moonbow genetics while preserving enough Hollywood Pure Kush and Do-Si-Dos influence to keep the flavor from becoming one-dimensional. The result can move from lemon candy and tangerine into perfume, incense, skunk, earth, and gas within the same session.

Its appeal extends beyond flower. Heavy resin production and a flavor profile capable of surviving extraction have helped Oishii earn a following in solventless cannabis, including award-winning concentrate releases from processors such as Wojo. For consumers interested in modern Z-influenced weed with more complexity than straightforward fruit candy, Oishii offers a convincing blend of contemporary sweetness, old-school Kush depth, gradual potency, and unusually persistent aroma.
